title: U.S. House · Oregon's 2nd District
area: Eastern, southern and much of rural Oregon, covering roughly 20 counties including Medford, Klamath Falls, Bend's eastern edges, and Ontario.

context.text: Incumbent Cliff Bentz defeated Peter Larson and Andrea Carr with 79.6% in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Chris Beck led a six-way Democratic primary field with 34.4% of the vote, ahead of Mary Doyle, Rebecca Mueller, Dawn Rasmussen, Patty Snow and Peter Quince; Ballotpedia noted this was the most-contested Oregon U.S. House primary field in 2026.

summary.text: Cliff Bentz is the Republican nominee for re-election to Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2021. A third-generation Oregonian raised on a family cattle ranch, he practiced water and ranch-reorganization law in Ontario for decades and served in both chambers of the Oregon Legislature before winning Congress in 2020.

background.text: Third-generation Oregonian, raised on his family's cattle ranches in Harney County; attended Regis High School near Salem, from which he graduated in 1970.
Graduated cum laude from Eastern Oregon State College (bachelor's degree in history and business, 1974) and earned a J.D. from Lewis and Clark Law School (1977).
Joined the Yturri, O'Kief, Rose and Burnham law firm in Ontario in 1977 and became a partner four years later, specializing in ranch reorganizations and water law.

While practicing law, served eight years as a member and then chair of the Oregon Water Resources Commission and as a director and chair of the Ontario 8C public school board; also served on the Project Dove (domestic violence prevention) board, the Eastern Oregon University Foundation Board and the Oregon Historical Society Board.

Was appointed to the Oregon House of Representatives (District 60) in January 2008, was elected that year, and served five two-year terms, including on the Revenue, Transportation, Energy and Environment and Joint Tax Credits committees.

Resigned from the Oregon House in 2018 when appointed to the Oregon Senate (District 30), where he served on the Finance and Revenue, Judiciary, Energy and Joint Tax Credits committees; resigned January 2, 2020, to campaign full-time for Congress.
Was elected to the U.S. House on November 3, 2020, and took office in 2021; won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 79.6% of the vote.
In the 119th Congress, serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on Natural Resources, with subcommittee assignments listed on Ballotpedia.
In 1987 married Dr. Lindsay Norman, a veterinarian who practices small animal medicine in Ontario, according to his official biography.

positions.summary: In an August 2025 OPB interview defended the budget law's Medicaid changes, saying they slow the program's growth and that people above the income limit should not be covered.
positions.quote: What we’re doing is barely slowing the growth of the program.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Health; Energy) and the Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Federal Lands; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries).

In the 118th Congress (2023-2024), chaired the House Natural Resources Committee's Subcommittee on Water, Oceans, and Wildlife and served on the House Judiciary Committee (Subcommittees on Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust; Courts, Intellectual Property, and the Internet).

As an Oregon state senator (2019-2020), served as Vice-Chair of the Senate Finance and Revenue Committee and Co-Vice Chair of the Tax Expenditures Committee, and sat on the Joint Transportation Committee, the Environment and Natural Resources Committee, and the Judiciary and Ballot Measure 110 Implementation Committee.

summary.text: Chris Beck is the Democratic (and Independent Party of Oregon) nominee for Oregon's 2nd Congressional District. A former state legislator from Phoenix, he worked in rural land-use and conservation and later as a rural economic policy adviser at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. He says his priorities include rural health care access, affordability and land-use planning.

background.text: Says he was born in Portland and attended public schools; graduated from Jackson High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Brown University in 1985 and graduated from Harvard University's Kennedy School of Government in 2005.

Began his career as legislative staff in the Oregon Legislature; news reports also say he worked for John Kitzhaber when Kitzhaber was Senate president and for Earl Blumenauer when Blumenauer was a Portland city councilor.

Worked for more than a decade for rural land-use and conservation nonprofits, including as a land-conservation real estate negotiator with the Trust for Public Land, helping conserve land in the Columbia Gorge and elsewhere in Oregon.
Served three terms in the Oregon House of Representatives (1997-2003), representing House District 12 in Lane County.
After the Legislature, spent six years as a rural economic policy adviser at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Washington, D.C., during the Obama administration.
Won the six-candidate May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 34.4% of the vote; described by the Oregon Capital Chronicle as living in Phoenix.

priorities.text: Health care access: describes quality health care as a human right and cites rural hospital and clinic closures making basic and emergency care harder to reach in the district.

Housing: says the free market alone has never produced affordable housing and calls for public assistance and incentives, with low-cost housing built into existing Main Street neighborhoods rather than on farm and forest land.

Trade and immigration: opposes the tariffs imposed during the Trump administration, which he says have hurt rural export markets, and calls for repealing them alongside a 'sensible, bipartisan approach to legal immigration.'

positions.summary: Says the current administration, 'with the blind support of our Congressman,' has cut Medicaid with no plan for comprehensive health care reform, and calls quality health care a human right.
positions.quote: Quality Health Care is a Human Right.

positions.summary: Calls the tariffs imposed under the Trump administration 'careless and haphazard' and says he would work to repeal them.

record.text: Voted no on HB 2744-A (prohibiting local governments from setting minimum wages above the statewide rate, except for public employers and contracts), which passed the Oregon House 36-22 on April 25, 2001.
Voted no on HB 2092-A (defining and expanding the scope of home visits and searches by probation officers), which passed the Oregon House 37-23 on February 6, 2001.

Voted no on HB 2010-A (authorizing environmental cleanup districts funded by a privilege tax on gross receipts, aimed at the Portland Harbor Superfund site), which passed the Oregon House 31-29 on June 4, 2001.
